items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Nothing is recommended, and L's weak axes are visible where it is leaned on: 870 ms pooled p95, a 0.3-point multi-hop clearance on a point estimate, best of eighteen. But our_lean picks the latency budget as 'the line to put to the planner's owner, since L misses only that one'. That reason applies equally to J, which misses only the pass line as far as the snapshot shows. The report's own figures cut the other way. L is at least 270 ms (45%) over the budget in some task, and that miss is certain. J's misses are 1.4 and 0.6 points, and on the watch slot's own inference those are about 1.2 and 0.4 SE (about 300 and 180 cases), so J's ambiguous-entity miss is as fragile as L's clearance. J costs $1,208 a month against L's $2,532. L and J aren't separated on pass rate over all tasks (compare L minus J reads -0.4 to +2.1). The direction of the lean is framed stronger than anything on the page supports.

items.reason: c1: a per-task dot plot against 97% and range bars against 600 ms are the right blocks, and flipping any value in L's, F's or J's rows would change c1. c2: cost bars now hold only L and F, and the per-task plot shows both above the line; the overall difference interval is in the prose and the caption says so. c3: a per-task plot of the six Brisk-S arms carries 'only high with a retry reaches the line in every task' (K at 95.5/96.6/96.1). c4: one frozen failure per task, first frozen and not chosen, which the caption states; the claim describes those two cases rather than a measured rate.

findings.finding: our_lean's reason doesn't discriminate. 'The latency budget is the line to put to the owner, since L misses only that one' holds just as well for J and the pass line. The page's figures point at least as much toward J. L misses the budget by at least 270 ms (870 vs 600, pooled, certain to be over in some task). J misses multi-hop by 1.4 and ambiguous entity by 0.6 points, and by the watch slot's own inference those are about 1.2 and 0.4 SE. J costs $1,208 a month against L's $2,532. L and J aren't separated on pass rate over all tasks (compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval reads -0.4 to +2.1). Either give a reason that favours the budget (for example, an owner statement that latency is the softer line), or state the lean as 'which line gives is the owner's call' and put the L-vs-J cost, latency and pass-rate figures side by side for it.

The routing option in where_it_flips says 'J clears single lookup and date math'. J's date-math rate is exactly on the line (criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.datemath.gap reads 0), so the routed mix's date-math clearance is borderline. The watch slot says so for J alone, but the routing sentence doesn't. Qualify it where routing is offered.

The claim describes J's misses ('it collapses a two-hop question into one query, and answers an ambiguous name without asking') from one frozen failure per task. examples_list holds exactly one J failure each in multi-hop and ambiguous entity. Make it explicit in the claim, not only the caption, that these are single examples, not the measured share of J's misses.

Prose outside the {arm:} keys names arms in a different form ('Brisk-S low retry', 'Brisk-S high retry', 'Atlas-M high without a retry', 'Atlas-M low retry') from the page's printed names ('Brisk-S · reasoning low · 1 retry (J)'). Use the arm keys, or at least the letter tags, in omitted and next so a reader can match them to the charts.
